results.reader_title: Scenario planning builds shared meaning
results.reader_what: Qualitative cases suggest futures workshops first create shared cognitive frames and can foster new collaborative relationships.
results.reader_why: Scenario workshops can be evaluated for social-capital development as well as strategic insights.
results.reader_more: Lang and Ramírez analyse three cases from two organisations: the European Patent Office and two Open University scenario exercises. They identify a mechanism by which joint work on alternative futures produces shared frames, language and other cognitive resources, enabling relational and network ties. This is qualitative foresight-method insight, not a measured effect size.

deep_analysis.research_question: How can scenarios create collective cognitive social capital and why is that a useful evaluation criterion?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Shared scenarios build cognitive social capital through meaning-making, then help social ties and cooperative structures form.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Original qualitative case analysis of European Patent Office and two separate UK Open University scenario-planning rounds.
deep_analysis.qualification: Three organisational cases, principally the European Patent Office and UK Open University; small qualitative sample limits generality of the mechanism.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: A reusable foresight facilitation and assessment mechanism, not simply a European organisation case study.

claims.qualification: Three organisational cases, principally the European Patent Office and UK Open University; small qualitative sample limits generality of the mechanism.
claims.text: The scenario-planning study suggests shared future narratives build cognitive social capital before relational and network ties emerge.
